note: Operations and general-management lens. Figures are company-reported for the period shown (Q2 FY27 = quarter to 30 Sep 2026, H1 FY27 = six months to 30 Sep 2026, FY26 = year to 31 Mar 2026). Where sources disagree or a number is not disclosed, the card says so. Process steps are generalised from how each model works; they are not internal documents.

operations.name: Ports and logistics (APSEZ)
operations.question: How does a port turn ships into revenue, and where does it lose time?
flow: Vessel plans a call; the port berth planner allocates a berth and tide window
Pilotage, tug and mooring; berthing begins (the PCS upgrade cut pre-operation berthing time by 24%, per company)
Cargo is discharged or loaded: conveyors for coal, cranes for containers, pipelines and tanks for liquids
Yard and storage: dwell time, stacking, customs clearance and inland evacuation by rail or road
Billing on volume (per tonne or TEU) and on services; marine and logistics add their own revenue lines

kpis.src: Ask the ports team for the internal figure

levers: Berth and tide-window planning (more ships per berth)
Yard dwell time and evacuation speed (rail and road)
Commodity mix: coal, containers, liquids, RoRo
Volume growth in the hinterland rather than tariff increases
bottlenecks: Rail and road evacuation from the port gate
Tide windows and weather at deep-draft berths
Customs and documentation delays
Dredging and berth maintenance downtime
operations.systems: Port community systems and a central monitoring hub (company calls it an AI-driven information hub, with NAVIS-based planning that the company says unlocked about 10% capacity).
operations.ask: What is the average turnaround time per vessel at Mundra, and what share of cargo leaves by rail?

operations.name: Airport operations (AAHL)
operations.question: How does an airport make money from more than the landing fee?
flow: Airline schedules and slots set aircraft movements (ATMs)
Passengers pass security, immigration and check-in; the government sets service-level benchmarks for each step
Aero revenue comes from regulated charges (set by AERA) per passenger and per aircraft movement
Non-aero revenue comes from retail, food and beverage, duty free, car parks, lounges, advertising and leases
City-side land and real estate develop around the terminal over time

kpis.v: 95% of peak passengers wait under 20 min (economy)
kpis.src: AEL Q1 FY27 investor deck, operational efficiency

levers: Passenger throughput per gate and per security lane
Non-aero spend per passenger (food, retail, parking)
Airline mix and route launches (8 new routes in Q2)
Cargo handling growth
bottlenecks: Peak-hour queues at security and immigration
Airline slot constraints and fuel prices
Ramp-up of a new airport such as Navi Mumbai, where costs run ahead of traffic
Aircraft movement rules and airspace restrictions
operations.systems: Passenger processing data, queue measurement at each checkpoint, and concession management for retail and F&B partners.
operations.ask: How does non-aero income per passenger differ between a mature airport and Navi Mumbai during ramp-up?

operations.name: Thermal power (Adani Power)
operations.question: What decides whether a thermal plant earns its capacity charge?
flow: Long-term PPA or PSA supplies contracted capacity; merchant and short-term sales fill the rest
Coal is bought (domestic linkage or imported) and moved by rail or conveyor to the plant
Boilers and turbines generate power; availability and heat rate determine efficiency
Power is dispatched to the grid by the load despatch centre, and billed as capacity plus energy charges
Ash is sold or used by cement makers; fuel costs are passed through under most PPAs

kpis.v: 70.1% in Q2 FY27 (62.8% a year ago); 67% in FY26
kpis.src: APL Q2 FY27 release; FY26 from APL FY26 results

kpis.v: ₹10,229 cr, up 41.8% (imported coal landed cost up about 50%)

levers: Plant availability (fewer forced outages)
PLF, which is driven by contracted and merchant demand
Coal sourcing mix: linkage, imports, blending
Merchant versus PPA sales mix
Ash utilisation, which earns revenue from cement makers
bottlenecks: Imported coal prices and freight
Forced outages on ageing units
Grid evacuation for new capacity
Demand swings and weather (monsoon affects hydro and demand)
operations.systems: Plant monitoring and AI-enabled O&M (the company describes predictive maintenance, anomaly detection and SCADA-based monitoring).
operations.ask: How much of the Q2 fuel-cost increase did PPA pass-through recover, and what did it leave on the company's books?

operations.name: Renewables (AGEL)
operations.question: How does a renewable portfolio keep generating after it is built?
flow: Land and grid connection are secured, then solar, wind or hybrid plants are built in large parks (Khavda is the anchor)
Plants are commissioned and sell energy under 25-year PPAs at fixed tariffs
A remote operations centre monitors plants in 12 states; predictive maintenance reduces failures
Generation is delivered to the grid; transmission and curtailment decide how much is actually sold
Storage (battery and pumped hydro) adds firm output when the grid can take it
levers: Plant availability and O&M response time (MTBF and MTTR)
Grid access, so curtailment does not cut sales
Build speed: capacity added per quarter
Storage that turns intermittent output into firm supply
Cost of capital on large capex
bottlenecks: Transmission and grid access (the company reports delayed grid access as a reason solar output fell short)
Curtailment by the grid operator during daytime peaks
Land and environmental approvals (Tarali is the live example)
Module and equipment supply chain
operations.systems: Energy network operations centre in Ahmedabad (real-time monitoring of 12 states), predictive-maintenance tools, and an industrial-cloud partnership for analytics.
operations.ask: How much generation is lost to grid curtailment each quarter, and does the company have a plan to recover it?

operations.name: Transmission and smart meters (AESL)
operations.question: How does a grid company earn fixed returns, and what breaks its schedules?
flow: A transmission project is won by competitive bidding (TBCB) with an annual tariff for about 35 years
Land rights, forest and environmental clearances, then construction of lines and substations
Commissioning, then the asset is availability-tested (the regulator pays for availability)
In Mumbai, the distribution business (AEML) buys, delivers and bills power, and manages losses
Smart meters are installed on a rollout schedule under state and central programmes
levers: Construction pace and capex deployment (transmission capex up 1.7x in H1 FY27)
Availability of lines, since tariffs depend on it
Distribution losses and collection efficiency (100.28% in Q2)
Meter installation per month against the rollout schedule
bottlenecks: Right-of-way and forest clearances
Supply of transformers and conductors
Installer capacity and consumer acceptance for smart meters
Payment discipline of state distribution companies
operations.systems: Substation monitoring, SCADA for lines, and meter-data management for the smart-meter base.
operations.ask: Which of the 15 transmission projects is most at risk of delay, and what is the cause?

operations.name: City gas (ATGL)
operations.question: How does a city gas network grow, and what can it not control?
flow: Gas is sourced: domestic allocation, long and medium-term LNG or pipeline contracts, and spot market purchases
Gas is delivered into the city network through steel pipelines to CNG stations and PNG homes
CNG stations sell fuel to vehicles; PNG meters bill households and industries
New areas are opened through government-awarded geographical areas (GAs)
Pricing is set by regulation for some segments, so input-cost shocks can squeeze margins
levers: Gas sourcing mix and cost pass-through
Station utilisation and new station roll-out
Industrial and commercial connections (higher-volume customers)
Network expansion into new geographical areas
bottlenecks: Gas availability and price (the company cites elevated prices from the West Asia crisis and rupee weakness)
Government allocation of domestic gas (a revised framework took effect from 5 July 2026)
Road digging permits and pipeline construction time
Competition for CNG demand from electric vehicles
operations.systems: Gas dispatch and SCADA for the network, customer billing for PNG, and station-level sales data.
operations.ask: What share of gas cost is passed through to customers within a quarter, and what is the lag?

operations.name: Cement (Ambuja, ACC)
operations.question: Why is cement a cost game, and what does a plant manager control?
flow: Limestone is quarried and crushed, then fed to a kiln to make clinker (the most energy-intensive step)
Clinker is ground with gypsum and blended materials into cement, either in an integrated plant or a grinding unit close to the market
Cement is dispatched by road, rail or ship (captive ships and bulk terminals), mostly to trade channels
Kiln fuel (coal, petcoke, alternative fuels) and power (green power share) drive the cost per tonne
Each plant's cost per tonne is compared across the network to decide where to add capacity
levers: Clinker factor (less clinker per tonne of cement)
Lead distance: grind near the market
Green power share and kiln fuel mix (alternative fuels)
Premium and blended product share
Fixed-cost absorption through plant utilisation
bottlenecks: Petcoke, coal and diesel prices; constrained coal availability
Monsoon-related demand loss in Q2
Long clinker haul where grinding units are far from kilns
Equipment lead times for new lines
operations.systems: Plant cost reporting per tonne and per '000 kcal, and fleet logistics tracking for trucks and ships.
operations.ask: What is the cost gap between the cheapest and the most expensive plant per tonne, and what would close it?

operations.name: Copper smelter (Kutch Copper)
operations.question: How does a smelter make a margin when its feed costs swing?
flow: Copper feed is bought as concentrate, scrap or recycled anode, and moved to the Mundra complex by sea or rail
Smelting and refining produce copper cathode; cast rods are made for cable makers
By-products are recovered: sulphuric acid, gold, silver and selenium
Product is sold to cable, transmission and industrial buyers; BIS certification and LME registration support pricing
Utilisation drives fixed-cost absorption; the plant ramps up in stages

kpis.v: 500 KTPA, with a route to 1 MTPA
~64% in Q2 FY27 (company figure; the Aug 2026 deck quoted ~52% for an earlier quarter)
80.6 KT in Q2 (5.8x YoY); 145.3 KT in H1

levers: Feedstock procurement and its price (concentrate, scrap, recycled material)
Utilisation ramp-up
By-product value (acid, precious metals)
Power cost (green power helps)
bottlenecks: Reliable feed supply, since copper concentrate is largely imported
Commodity price swings and treatment charges
Ramp-up of a new smelter, with quality approvals from customers
operations.systems: Lab quality control with NABL-accredited assays for precious metals, and plant-level production and by-product reporting.
operations.ask: How much of the feed is locked in under contracts, and how much is bought on the spot market?

operations.name: Solar and wind manufacturing (ANIL)
operations.question: How does a manufacturer move from factory capacity to sold output?
flow: Ingots and wafers (2 GW operational), then cells (4 GW operational, 6 GW more due by FY27 end), then modules (10 GW line)
Wind turbine generators are assembled from blades, towers and nacelles, and listed under the government's approved model list
Output is sold to group developers (AGEL) first and third parties second, with domestic content rules applying
Lines are commissioned in stages; output lags nameplate capacity during ramp-up
Export offtake is balanced against domestic demand

kpis.v: 4 GW operational; 6 GW due by FY27 end
2,818 MW (+15% YoY); Q2 1,478 MW, all domestic

levers: Cell capacity, which is the bottleneck behind module output
Utilisation of each line during ramp-up
Domestic content compliance, which secures demand
Export mix
bottlenecks: Module capacity has been built faster than cell capacity
Equipment supplied from abroad and commissioning time
Price competition from imported modules
operations.systems: Line-level production tracking, quality testing, and approved-model lists for wind turbines.
operations.ask: When the 6 GW cell line is commissioned, what is the expected utilisation for the first year?

operations.name: Data centres (AdaniConneX)
operations.question: How fast can a data-centre company turn signed capacity into live megawatts?
flow: A hyperscale customer signs for capacity in megawatts of IT load, usually years before delivery
Land, grid connection and power purchase are secured first
Core and shell (buildings) are built, then mechanical and electrical fit-out (MEP)
Capacity is handed over to the customer in phases
Uptime and efficiency are managed against service-level agreements

kpis.v: 1.2+ GW (including a 240 MW Navi Mumbai order)

kpis.src: Ask the team for PUE and its trend

levers: Delivery speed: MW handed over per quarter
Power sourcing (renewable supply from the group)
Land and grid readiness for the next site
Cooling and PUE efficiency
bottlenecks: Grid connection and substation timelines
Equipment lead times for electrical gear
Construction in phases while live customers are operating
Power procurement at scale
operations.systems: Building management systems, power monitoring and SLA reporting to customers.
operations.ask: Is delivery measured per phase or per megawatt, and how far is the Navi Mumbai build behind plan?

mindset: A general manager owns a P&L across functions, so you must see how a decision in one function moves cost or revenue in another.
Start every discussion from the operating metric, then the financial impact, then the decision. Not the other way round.
Always say what you would measure in the first 90 days, and who you would ask for the data.

pnl_tree.title: Driver tree for any business

kids: Price or yield (tariff, cost per tonne, income per passenger)

pnl_tree.use: Pick the branch with the biggest unexplained change. Ask which operating metric moved it.

memo.title: The one-page operations memo
sections: Situation: what changed, with the number and period
Diagnosis: which driver moved and why (one chart)
Options: at least two, each with cost, time and risk
Recommendation and the metric that proves it worked
Owner, date and the decision you need

first30: Get the business's KPI pack for the last eight quarters and the plan for the year
Walk the process on the ground: a plant, port berth, station or site office
Meet the five people who own each step in the flow (ops, maintenance, finance, procurement, customer)
Map the top three bottlenecks and the data you need to size each one
Write the first problem statement and agree it with your mentor by day 30
mentor_questions: Which one number do you check first every morning, and why?
What did the last intern get wrong about this business?
Where are the decisions in this business made, and who makes them?
What would make you say a project failed, and at what point?

frameworks.d: Output divided by available capacity. Fixed costs are spread over more units as utilisation rises, so small utilisation gains can have large margin effects.
Days of receivables plus inventory minus days of payables. Cutting it frees cash without any change to profit.
Revenue per unit minus variable cost per unit, times volume, minus fixed cost. Compare a business's unit economics with its nearest competitor's.
Payback = investment divided by annual cash flow. Also check IRR and NPV at the company's cost of capital.
Find the step with the lowest throughput. Raising output anywhere else does not raise total output.

cases.title: Tarali pumped storage: a permit and a cost question
cases.setup: The forest department halted work at AGEL's 1,500 MW Tarali pumped-storage project (13 November 2026). It says work started before the wildlife board's approval. Separately, a cost estimate of ₹5,675 crore was revised to ₹56.75 crore in a filing to the forest department, which reduces the conservation deposit. AGEL says all statutory clearances were obtained and no protected area is involved.
cases.question: You are an operations and general management intern on the project team. What do you do in the first week?
strong_answer_covers: Separate the two issues: the permit sequence and the cost filing, which need different owners
Map the approvals timeline: what was cleared, when, and what is pending at the wildlife board
Cost the delay: stoppage days, idle contractors, financing carry
Recommend a single source of truth for documents before any further filing
Name the stakeholders: forest department, state government, lenders, contractors, local villagers
cases.src: Indian Express and India Today reports, 16–17 Nov 2026; AGEL statement

cases.title: Smart-meter rollout: why not faster?
cases.setup: AESL has installed 14.8 million smart meters and holds an orderbook of 24.6 million meters with a revenue potential of about ₹29,500 crore. In Q2 it installed 1.3 million, down from 1.8 million a year earlier.
cases.question: The rollout is behind a plan you were given. Where do you look first, and what would you change?
strong_answer_covers: Per-day installation rate by state, by installer and by month
Consumer acceptance and access issues (locked premises, disputes)
Installer capacity and training; meter and SIM supply
Payment and collection setup per state utility
A weekly dashboard with a clear owner per bottleneck
cases.src: AESL Q2 FY27 operational highlights and results release

cases.title: Evos integration: the first 100 days
cases.setup: APSEZ agreed on 5 November 2026 to buy Evos for €2.56 billion enterprise value. Evos runs eight terminals in five European countries with a 56% EBITDA margin. The company gave a 15-month indicative completion window, subject to approvals and works-council consultation.
cases.question: Completion is months away. What operating plan do you prepare before closing?
strong_answer_covers: Integration priorities: safety, customer contracts (take-or-pay), IT and reporting
What not to change in the first 100 days (operating teams, customer relationships)
Synergy list: procurement, shared services, commercial pricing
Governance: which decisions need head-office sign-off
Risks: labour consultation, regulatory conditions, currency exposure
cases.src: APSEZ Evos release and Reg. 30 disclosure, 5 Nov 2026

cases.title: Navi Mumbai airport: ramping up without losing the service standard
cases.setup: Navi Mumbai International Airport began commercial operations on 25 December 2025 and started international passenger services on 15 July 2026. Its passenger numbers are still building while the company carries a large fixed-cost base.
cases.question: How do you keep security and immigration queues within the benchmark while passenger numbers are still building?
strong_answer_covers: Queue measurement at each checkpoint, against the 95th-percentile benchmark
Staffing and lane-opening rules tied to forecast peaks
Airline schedule coordination to smooth arrival waves
Non-aero offers that move passengers away from peak queues
Cost of over-capacity versus the penalty for missing service levels
cases.src: AEL Q1 and Q2 FY27 investor decks

cases.title: Kutch Copper: feed, utilisation and a margin
cases.setup: The Mundra copper plant ran at about 64% of capacity in Q2 FY27, with sales up 5.8 times year on year. It buys feed that is largely imported and has agreed a recycled-copper supply deal reported at about $1 billion over three years.
cases.question: Utilisation is 64%. Would you push for higher output or look for a different constraint first?
strong_answer_covers: Check whether feed or the plant is the constraint before you push volume
Unit margin at each utilisation level, including by-product credits
Feed contract cover and price risk; spot versus term share
Quality and customer approvals as a gating step for new volume
A test plan: one pilot line or month before scaling
cases.src: AEL Q2 FY27 earnings call and investor deck; CNBC-TV18 report on the Attero deal

metrics_cheatsheet.d: Share of time a plant could run, regardless of whether it was dispatched. High availability with low PLF usually means weak demand, not a fault.
Fuel energy used per unit of electricity sent out. Lower is better. Coal plants are compared on this figure; the sources here do not disclose the fleet heat rate.
Clinker used per tonne of cement. A lower figure means cheaper cement, because clinker is the costliest step.
Average distance from the limestone mine to the plant. It drives freight cost.
Time from a vessel's arrival to its departure, or a truck's gate-in to gate-out. Shorter means more capacity from the same berth or gate.

metrics_cheatsheet.t: Yield per passenger (YPP) and income per passenger (IPP)
metrics_cheatsheet.d: Aero income per passenger (YPP) and non-aero income per passenger (IPP). They show how well an airport monetises each traveller.

metrics_cheatsheet.t: Mean time between failures and to repair (MTBF, MTTR)
metrics_cheatsheet.d: MTBF measures reliability; MTTR measures how fast a fault is fixed. Good O&M raises the first and cuts the second.
Availability times performance times quality. A manufacturing score of how much of a line's theoretical output is good output.
Receivable, inventory and payable days combined. Less cash tied up in the cycle means more free cash for the same profit.
Cost of the heat the kiln uses, in rupees per thousand kilocalories. The main cement cost lever after clinker factor.
